S061-01.notes: 'Only the person who tied them could interpret' defines idiosyncratic. A (numerical) contradicts the dismissal, since numbers are what researchers later found. B (standardized) is the opposite of the dismissal. D (ornamental) means decorative, not records only one person could read. The word itself is the main difficulty. Facts are accurate.

S061-02.notes: The arrowhead near a torn artery overturns the exposure assumption. B (storm) and D (escaping an attack) go beyond the text. C contradicts the torn artery. 'Not the cold alone' is suitably hedged. Facts check out: found 1991, about 5,300 years, arrowhead seen on X-ray in 2001 in the left shoulder near the torn subclavian artery.

S061-03.notes: The text runs from visitors to damage to closure and a replica. A is the opposite of what the text says, and B and C are not covered. Facts check out: about 17,000 years; opened 1948; about 1,200 visitors a day, so 'more than a thousand' is fine; closed 1963; replicas nearby (Lascaux II, and Lascaux IV today).

S061-04.notes: Text 2 says a body should be judged by its own nature (shape, geology), not by its surroundings. C is a trap: Text 2 does not dispute the facts about the clearing test, only whether the test is relevant. A agrees with Text 1. D is extreme, since Text 2 keeps the requirement of planet-like features. The IAU 2006 definition is stated accurately.

S061-05.notes: A colon after a full independent clause introduces the list. B: a semicolon cannot come before a fragment. C: a colon after 'including' splits the verbal phrase from its object. D: with no punctuation, the list runs on into the clause. Each option was inserted and checked.

S061-06.notes: 'By the time ... closed' (past) calls for the past perfect. A, B and D give the wrong tense. 'Algae' is grammatically plural, but no option depends on that except A, which fails on tense anyway.

S061-07.notes: People keep calling it a planet despite the reclassification, which is a concession, so 'Nevertheless'. A gives the reverse logic. B and C do not fit the relationship.

S061-08.notes: Only B shows both the first view (exposure) and the later view (a wound), which is the change in understanding. A, C and D each give only a single point in time. 'A 2001 arrowhead find' is a little compressed, since an X-ray revealed it, but it is accurate enough.

S061-09.notes: Old way (walking between drawers) versus new way (online in seconds) is a contrast. 'As a result' implies cause, but the drawers did not cause online search. A and C do not fit.

S061-10.notes: Only A states the limitation (no negative, so no reproduction). B, C and D give neutral history or process facts. Facts check out: announced in France in 1839, silver-coated copper plates, no negative, each image unique. The answer is fairly obvious, which is typical of rhetorical-synthesis items and not a defect.
